- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in following 7–14 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model may lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 3–5 day mean, not peak.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model often fails to reverse; apply early mean-reversion correction (e.g., 1–2% drop in 3–5 days).
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overfit recent volatility; use 10–15 day rolling average as baseline for smoothing.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model often misjudges direction; favor sentiment-weighted average of last 7–10 days over pure trend.
